This is gonna be our families first attempt. Going for Salad Greens mostly. Was curious if anyone else has ever tried on here and could share some experience.
Anybody gonna try a fall garden?

Salad greens are easy, watch out for bugs and slugs. Personal favorite is kohlrabi though, just peel and eat it, firm and sweet. Even the kids scream for more. Also, when you cut it, it will grow two on the old root stock so don't tear it out. This happens till heat or heavy freeze does it in.

I always chuckle at the preppers who buy seeds, like that's enough. Takes a lot more than seeds to learn how to grow things and feed yourself, some fertilizer and pest management and rabbit fencing should be added. Then there is learning food preservation, as eating for 4 months out of the year won't cut it.

On that note, try some Swiss chard. Grows well in anything but hot or freezing temps, easy to harvest the big ones and new shoots pop up. Blanch and vacuum pack and freeze and you have good nutrition to last the whole year. Try stuffed in chicken breast with some goat cheese.

Carrots are another good one, easy to grow, takes little space, saves in the ground all winter or in a root cellar in wet sand till spring time. If they don't taste good or are spicy, add dolomite lime to your soil.
